pp:ee:2013:q2.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ee:2013:q2.question: The transfer function $\frac{V_{2}(s)}{V_{1}(s)}$ of the circuit shown below is

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems
detailed_solution.markdown: $\frac{V_2(s)}{V_1(s)}=\frac{R+\frac{1}{Cs}}{\frac{1}{Cs}+R+\frac{1}{Cs}}$ $=\frac{1+RCs}{2+RCs}$ $=\frac{1+10 \times 10^3 \times 100 \times 10^{-6}s}{2+10 \times 10^3 \times 100 \times 10^{-6}s}$ $=\frac{s+1}{s+2}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ee:2013:q3.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ee:2013:q3.question: Assuming zero initial condition, the response y(t) of the system given below to a unit step input u(t) is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Y(s)&=\frac{1}{s}U(s)=\frac{1}{s^2}\\ y(t)&=tu(t) \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q4.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:ee:2013:q4.question: The impulse response of a system is h(t)=tu(t). For an input u(t-1), the output is

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} h(t) &=tu(t) \\ H(s) &=\frac{1}{s^2} \\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{Y(s)}{U(s)} &=\frac{1}{s^2} \\ Y(s) &=\frac{1}{s^2} \frac{e^{-s}}{s}\\ \Rightarrow \; y(t) &=\frac{(t-1)^2}{2}u(t-1) \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q6.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 6

pp:ee:2013:q7.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 7
pp:ee:2013:q7.question: A source $v_{s}(t)=V \cos 100\pi t$ has an internal impedance of $(4+j3)\Omega$. If a purely resistive load connected to this source has to extract the maximum power out of the source, its value in $\Omega$ should be

$R_L=|Z|=|4-j3|$

$\;\;=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5\Omega$

pp:ee:2013:q9.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 9
pp:ee:2013:q9.question:
A single-phase transformer has no-load loss of 64W, as obtained from an open
circuit test. When a short-circuit test is performed on it with 90% of the rated
currents flowing in its both LV and HV windings, he measured loss is 81 W. The
transformer has maximum efficiency when operated at

detailed_solution.markdown:
For 90% current,

$$\begin{aligned} P_{cu} &=(0.9)^2 P_{fl\;cu} \\ P_{fl\;cu} &= \frac{81}{0.81}=100W\\ x&=\sqrt{\frac{P_{core}}{P_{fl\;cu}}}=\sqrt{\frac{64}{100}}=0.8=80\% \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q10.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 10
pp:ee:2013:q10.question: The flux density at a point in space is given by $B=4xa_{x}+2kya_{y}+8a_{z} Wb/m^{2}$. The value of constant k must be equal to

pp:ee:2013:q13.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 13
pp:ee:2013:q13.question: In the feedback network shown below, if the feedback factore k is increased, then the
options: The input impedance increases and output impedance decreases
The input impedance increases and output impedance also increases
The input impedance decreases and output impedance also decreases
The input impedance decreases and output impedance increases

detailed_solution.concept: Analog Electronics - Oscillators and Feedback Amplifiers

The given configuration is a voltage-series feedback configuration.

So, the input impedance  increases

pp:ee:2013:q15.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 15
pp:ee:2013:q15.question:
The Bode plot of a transfer function G(s) is shown in the figure below.

The gain (20 log|G(s)| is 32 dB and -8 dB at 1 rad/s and 10 rad/s respectively. The phase is negative for all $\omega$. Then G(s) is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let,  $G(s)=\frac{K}{s^n}$

$G(j\omega )=\frac{K}{(j\omega )^n}$

$\because$  Gain=32 dB at $\omega =1$ rad/sec

$\therefore \; 20log\left | \frac{K}{1^n} \right |=32$

$\Rightarrow \; 20 log K=32$

$\Rightarrow \; K=39.8$

$Now,$

$\because \;$ Gain=-8 dB at $\omega =10$ rad/sec

$\therefore \; 20log\left | \frac{39.8}{10^n} \right |=-8$

$\Rightarrow \; 10^n=100$

$\Rightarrow \; n=2$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q19.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 19
pp:ee:2013:q19.question: Consider a delta connection of resistors and its equivalent star connection as shown below. If all elements of the delta connection are scaled by a factor $k , k\gt 0$, the elements of the corresponding star equivalent will be scaled by a factor of

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Basics of Electric Circuit
detailed_solution.markdown:
$R_A=\frac{R_bR_c}{R_a+R_b+R_c}$

$R'_a=kR_a$

$R'_b=kR_b$

$R'_c=kR_c$

$R'_A=\frac{kR_b\cdot kR_c}{kR_a+kR_b+kR_c}$

$\;\;=\frac{k^2R_bR_c}{k(R_a+R_b+R_c)}$

$\;\;=k \times \frac{R_bR_c}{R_a+R_b+R_c}$

$R'_A=kR_A$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q28.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ee:2013:q28.question: The open-loop transfer function of a dc motor is given as $\frac{\omega (s)}{V_a(s)}=\frac{10}{1+10s}$. When connected in feedback as shown below, the approximate value of $K_a$ that will reduce the time constant of the closed loop system by one hundred times as compared to that of the open-loop system is

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Feedback Characteristics of Control Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\omega (s)}{V_a(s)}=\frac{10}{1+10s}=\frac{10}{1+\tau s}$

$\tau =10$

Closed loop systems,

$\frac{\omega (s)}{R(s)}=\frac{\frac{10K_a}{1+10s}}{1+\frac{10K_a}{1+10s}}$

$=\frac{10K_a}{1+10K_a+10s}$

$=\frac{\frac{10K_a}{1+10K_a}}{1+\frac{10}{1+10K_a}s}$

According to quetion,

$\frac{10}{1+10K_a}=\frac{1}{100}\times 10$

$1+10K_a=100$

$K_a=9.9$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

detailed_solution.markdown: $V_{L_1}=\left ( \frac{j4}{3+j4} \right )100\angle 53.13^{\circ}$ $\;\;=80\angle 90^{\circ}V$ $V_{Th}=10V_{L_1}=800\angle 90^{\circ}V$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q30.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 30
pp:ee:2013:q30.question: Three capacitors $C_1, C_2 \; and \; C_3$ whose values are 10 $\mu$F, 5 $\mu$F, and 2 $\mu$F respectively, have breakdown voltages of 10 V, 5 V and 2 V respectively. For the interconnection shown below, the maximum safe voltage in Volts that can be applied across the combination, and the corresponding total charge in $\mu$C stored in the effective capacitance across the terminals are respectively,

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Basics of Electric Circuit
detailed_solution.markdown:
$Q=CV$

$Q_1=C_1V_1 =10 \times 10^{-6} \times 10=100\mu C$

$Q_2=C_2V_2 =5 \times 10^{-6} \times 5=25\mu C$

$Q_3=C_3V_3 =2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2=4\mu C$

Capacitor $C_2 \; and \; C_3$ are in series.

In series charge is same.

So, maximum charge on $C_2 \; and \; C_3$ will be minimum of

$(Q_2,Q_3)=min(25\mu C,4\mu C)=4\mu C=Q_{23}$.

In series the equivalent capacitance of $C_2 \; and \; C_3$ is

$C_{23}=\frac{C_2C_3}{C_2+C_3}=\frac{5 \times 2}{5+2}=\frac{10}{7}\mu F$

So, equivalent voltage,

$V_{23}=\frac{Q_{23}}{C_{23}}=\frac{4 \times 10^{-6}}{\frac{10}{7} \times 10^{-6}}=\frac{28}{10}2.8V$

In parallel, the voltage is same.

$V_1=V_{23}=2.8V$

Change in capacitor $C_1$

$Q_1=C_1V_1 =10 \times 10^{-6}\times 2.8=28\mu C$

In parallel, the total charge

$Q=Q_1+Q_{23}$

$Q=4+28=32\mu C$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q34.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ee:2013:q34.question: A dielectric slab with 500 mm x 500 mm cross-section is 0.4 m long. The slab is subjected to a uniform electric field of $E=6a_{x}+8a_{y}$ kV/mm. The relative permittivity of the dielectric material is equal to 2. The value of constant $\varepsilon _{0} \; is\;  8.85\times 10^{-12}$ F/m. The energy stored in the dielectric in Joules is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Energy density $=\frac{1}{2}\in |\vec{E}|^2$

Energy = Energy density x Volume

Energy $=\frac{1}{2} \times \in _0 \times \in _r(6^2+8^2)\times 10^{12}$  $\times 0.5 \times 0.5 \times 0.5$

$=\frac{1}{2} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 2 \times 100 \times 10^{12} \times 0.1$

$=88.5 J$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q35.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ee:2013:q35.question: A Matrix has eigenvalues -1 and -2. The corresponding eigenvectors are $$\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix} and \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}$$ respectively. The matrix is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} AX &=\lambda X \\ \begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix}&=(-1) \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -1 \end{bmatrix}\\ a-b&= -1\\ c-d&=1 \\ \begin{bmatrix} a & b\;\;...(i)\\ c & d\;\;...(ii) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}&=(-2) \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ -2 \end{bmatrix}\\ a-2b&=-2\;\;...(iii) \\ c-2d&=4\;\;...(iv) \end{aligned}$$

From equation (i) and (iii), a=0 and  b=1

From equation (ii) and (iv), c=-2 and d=-3

$$A= \begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ c & d \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ee:2013:q36.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ee:2013:q36.question: $\oint \frac{z^{2}-4}{z^{2}+4}dz$ evaluated anticlockwise around the circle |z-i|=2, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, is

detailed_solution.markdown: $\frac{Z^2-4}{Z^2+4}=\frac{Z^2-4}{(Z+2i)(Z-2i)}$ Poles at 2i and -2i i.e. (0,2i) and (0,-2i) From figure of |Z-i|=2, we see that pole, is insice C. while pole, -2i is outside of C. $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \;\oint \frac{Z^2-4}{Z^2+4}dZ &=2 \pi i \times \text{Res.} \;F(Z)\\ &= \left.\begin{matrix} 2 \pi i \frac{(Z-2i)(Z^2-4)}{(Z+2i)(Z-2i)} \end{matrix}\right|_{Z=2i}\\ &= 2 \pi i\frac{(2i)^2 -4}{(2i+2i)}=-4 \pi \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ee:2013:q40.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ee:2013:q40.question: The signal flow graph for a system is given below. The transfer function $\frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}$ for this system is

detailed_solution.concept: Control Systems - Mathematical Models of Physical Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
Using mason's gain formula,

$\Delta =1-[-2s^{-1}-2s^{-2}-4-4s^{-1}]$

$\Delta =1+\frac{2}{s}+\frac{2}{s^2}+4+\frac{4}{s}$

$\Delta =\frac{5s^2+6s+2}{s^2}$

$P_1=s^{-2}=\frac{1}{s^2}$

$P_2=s^{-1}=\frac{1}{s}$

$\Delta _1=1$

$\Delta _2=2$

$\frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{\Sigma P_k\Delta _k}{\Delta }$

$\;\;\;\;=\frac{\frac{1}{s^2} \times 1+\frac{1}{s} \times 1}{\frac{5s^2+6s+2}{s^2}}$

$\frac{Y(s)}{U(s)}=\frac{s+1}{5s^2+6s+2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ee:2013:q41.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ee:2013:q41.question: The impulse response of a continuous time system is given by $h(t)=\delta(t-1) \delta (t-3)$ . The value of the step response at t=2 is

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
For step response, impulse response can be integrated.

$$\begin{aligned} y(t)&=u(t-1)+u(t-3)\\ y(2)&=u(1)+u(-1)\\ &=1+0=1 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q42.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ee:2013:q42.question:
Two magnetically uncoupled inductive coils have Q factors $q_1 \; and \; q_2$ at the chosen
operating frequency. Their respective resistances are $R_1 \; and \; R_2$. When connected
in series, their effective Q factor at the same operating frequency is

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Resonance and Locus Diagrams
detailed_solution.markdown: $q_1=\frac{\omega L_1}{R_1}$ $L_1=\frac{q_1R_1}{\omega }$ Similarly, $L_2=\frac{q_2R_2}{\omega }$ $Q=\frac{\omega (L_1+L_2)}{R_1+R_2}$ $=\frac{q_1R_1+q_2R_2}{R_1+R_2}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q43.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ee:2013:q43.question: The following arrangement consists of an ideal transformer and an attenuator which attenuates by a factor of 0.8. An ac voltage $V_{WX1}$ = 100 V is applied across WX to get an open circuit voltage $V_{YZ1}$ across YZ. Next, an ac voltage$V_{YZ2}$ = 100 V is applied across YZ to get an open circuit voltage $V_{WX2}$ across WX. Then,$V_{YZ1}/V_{WX1},V_{WX2}/V_{YZ2}$ are respectively,

primary.subtopicLabel: Magnetically Coupled Circuits, Network Topology and Filters

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Magnetically Coupled Circuits, Network Topology and Filters
detailed_solution.markdown:
$V_{YZ_1}=100\times 1.25 \times 0.8 =100$

In second case when 100 V is applied at YZ terminals, this whole 100 V will appear across the secondary winding,

Hence, $V_{WX_2}=\frac{100}{1.25}=80V$

$\Rightarrow \; \frac{V_{YZ_1}}{V_{WX_1}}=\frac{100}{100}$

$\frac{V_{WX_2}}{V_{YZ_2}}=\frac{80}{100}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q45.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:ee:2013:q45.question:
A 4-pole induction motor, supplied by a slightly unbalanced three-phase 50 Hz
source, is rotating at 1440 rpm. The electrical frequency in Hz of the induced
negative sequence current in the rotor is

detailed_solution.concept: Electrical Machines - Three Phase Induction Machines
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} N_s &=\frac{120 \times 50}{14}=1500 \; \text{rpm} \\ s&= \frac{1500-1440}{1500}=0.04 \end{aligned}$$

For negative sequence component,

$$\begin{aligned} s'&=2-s \\ &=2-0.04=1.96 \\ f'&=s'f \\ &= 1.96 \times 50=98.00Hz \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q48.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:ee:2013:q48.question:
In the figure shown below, the chopper feeds a resistive load from a battery source. MOSFET Q is switched at 250 kHz, with a duty ratio of 0.4. All elements of the circuit are assumed to be ideal.

The average source current in Amps in steady-state is

detailed_solution.markdown:
As it is a boost converter, average current through capacitor is zero.

When Q is ON, $I_c=-I_0$

$I_c=I_s-I_0$

Therefore, average through capacitor

$$\begin{aligned} &=(-I_0)I_{ON}+(I_s-I_0)T_{OFF}=0 \\ &(-I_0)DT+(I_s-I_0)(1-D)T=0 \\ & -I_0D+I_s-I_sD-I_0+I_0D=0\\ &\Rightarrow \;\; I_0=(1-D)I_s\\ I_s&=\frac{I_0}{(1-D)}\\ &=\frac{V_0}{R(1-D)}\\ &=\frac{V_s}{R(1-D)^2}\\ &=\frac{12}{20(1-0.4)^2}=\frac{5}{3}A \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ee:2013:q49.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:ee:2013:q49.question:
In the figure shown below, the chopper feeds a resistive load from a battery source. MOSFET Q is switched at 250 kHz, with a duty ratio of 0.4. All elements of the circuit are assumed to be ideal.

The PEAK-TO-PEAK source current ripple in Amps is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Here,

$$\begin{aligned} I_{source}&=\text{Inductor current}\\ \because \;\; V&=L\frac{dI_s}{dt}\\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{V}{L}\int_{0}^{T_{ON}}dt&=\int_{min}^{max}dI_s\\ \Rightarrow \;\frac{V}{L}T_{ON}&=I_{s\; max}-I_{s \; min}\\ &= \text{ripple source current}\\ \Rightarrow \; T_{ON}&=D.T.\\ \therefore \; \text{ripple source current}&=\frac{V}{L}(D.T.)\\ &=\frac{12}{100 \times 10^{-6}}\times 0.4 \times \frac{1}{250 \times 10^3}\\ &=0.192A \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ee:2013:q50.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:ee:2013:q50.question:
The state variable formulation of a system is given as
$$\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x_1}\\ \dot{x_2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0&-1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}u$$ $$x_1(0)=0,x_2(0)=0\ and \; y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}$$
The system is
options: both not controllable and not observable

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$A=\begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \\ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix},$$  $$B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$AB=\begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \\ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2\\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$$

For controllability, $|B \; : \;\;AB|\neq 0$

$$\;\;\; \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2\\ 1& -1 \end{bmatrix}=-1-(-2)=1 \neq 0$$

The system is controllable.

$$C^T=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$A^TC^T=\begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 \\ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$

For observability, $[C^T\;: \; A^TC^T]\neq 0$

$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2\\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}=0$$

The system is not observable.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ee:2013:q51.title: GATE EE 2013 | Set 1 | Question: 51
pp:ee:2013:q51.question:
The state variable formulation of a system is given as
$$\begin{bmatrix} \dot{x_1}\\ \dot{x_2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0&-1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\1 \end{bmatrix}u$$ $$x_1(0)=0,x_2(0)=0\ and \; y=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\x_2 \end{bmatrix}$$
The response y(t) to the unit step input is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} [sI-A]&=\begin{bmatrix} s & 0\\ 0 &s \end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0\\ 0& -1 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} s+2 & 0\\ 0 &s+1 \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2} & 0\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}[B]&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2} & 0\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2}\\ \frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix} \\ C[sI-A]^{-1}[B]&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+2}\\ \frac{1}{s+1} \end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ G(s)&=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}&=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ Y(s)&=\frac{1}{s(s+2)}=\frac{1}{2}\left [ \frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+2} \right ] \\ y(t)&=\frac{1}{2}(1-e^{-2t})=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}e^{-2t} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.
